newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Eastern Australian grainbelt missed by heavy rain.
newsitem.headline: Eastern Australian grainbelt missed by heavy rain.

text.p: Heavy weekend rain along Australia's southeast coast failed to deliver for grains farmers west of the seaboard, weather officials said on Monday.
Now is a critical time for planting Australia's winter cereal crop, after a record or near-record dry spell in Australia's southeast states.
armers need rain in the next five weeks to proceed with the plant.

While 100 millimetres or more in weekend rain fell on many coastal areas in the main eastern wheat states of New South Wales (NSW) and Victoria, grains farmers west of the dividing mountain ranges received virtually no rain, officials in the two states' Bureaus of Meteorology told Reuters.
Dry conditions remained west of the ranges despite some falls there last week which broke record or near-record drought periods in many centres.
An official with the Victorian bureau said "not a great deal" of rain had fallen over the weekend on main grain growing areas of the state, with most weekend rain received in the East Gippsland area.

A spokesman for the NSW Bureau said NSW's grains areas received "nothing worth talking about" over the weekend, although Sydney received 100 millimetres in downpours which were "extremely variable" from centre to centre.
Coastal regions of Victoria and NSW on the weekend experienced efects from the same low.
Some rain could be received later this week in NSW, South Australia and western Queensland from a cloud mass moving over Australia from Western Australia, he said.

The Victorian Bureau said on Friday that southern Australia continued to experience serious to severe rainfall deficiency, while the NSW Bureau said the drought-delcared area of that state had been increased to 40 percent from 13 percent.
